name: Choice Hotels

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (Choice Hotels logo.svg, commons.wikimedia.org)

description: Choice is primarily a hotel franchisor: it licenses 22 brands (Comfort, Quality, Sleep Inn, Econo Lodge, Clarion, Ascend Collection, WoodSpring Suites, Radisson, Cambria and others) to owners of 7,575 open hotels with 656,825 rooms in 50 countries and territories, 76% of those rooms in the US. It earns royalties and fees that are a percentage of franchised hotels' room revenue ($673 million in 2025), plus fees from vendors and partners (credit-card and other partnerships, $114 million) and revenue from a small number of hotels it owns to launch newer brands (Cambria, Everhome Suites, $121 million). About $616 million of the $1.6 billion of 2025 revenue is reimbursement of costs for franchised and managed properties. Operating income was $448 million in 2025 and net income $370 million, including a $100 million gain from acquiring a joint venture; operating income fell in the first half of 2026.

sub.name: Hotels, resorts, theme parks and live events

gics.note: From Wikipedia 'List of S&P 400 companies' (raw wikitext read 2026-10-27; the table has only GICS Sector and GICS Sub-Industry columns, so industry group and industry are left null). The same page shows Choice joining the S&P MidCap 400 on December 10, 2019.

employees.note: 1,562 U.S. and 192 international associates, excluding employees at 13 managed hotels (FY2025 10-K Human Capital)

businessLines.name: Hotel Franchising & Management
businessLines.how: Hotel owners pay Choice an initial fee, then ongoing royalty, marketing and reservation fees that are percentages of the hotel's gross room revenue (outside the US often via master franchisees), so income rises with room count, RevPAR and royalty rate; partners pay for access to Choice's guests and franchisees.
businessLines.description: Franchise and management fees, partnership services and fees, other franchising revenue and reimbursed costs across the 22 brands.

businessLines.how: Room, food and other revenue from the few hotels Choice owns, which are run by third-party managers; the purpose is to speed up franchise sales of Cambria and Everhome Suites rather than to hold real estate long term.
businessLines.description: Owns 10 Cambria, four Everhome Suites, one Radisson RED, one Radisson Blu and one Country Inn & Suites hotels (17 in all) to help launch newer brands; plans to sell them to franchisees under long-term Choice franchise agreements.
